title: Popeye the Sailor
paragraphs: Frozen GRH snapshot contains twelve files but only six unique recordings: four genuine 1930s radio programs plus two later kiddie/commercial record items. Every title appears twice as an alternate transfer/encode.

GRH documents the program through NBC Red / Wheatena run (September 10, 1935 to March 28, 1936) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], WABC / Wheatena run (August 31, 1936 to February 26, 1937) on [[org|org.b1c76a6702c1bee9|WABC]], and CBS / Popsicle run (May 2, 1938 to July 29, 1938) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Anne Hummert (producer on 8 recordings), Charles Lawrence (performer on 8 recordings), Elzie Segar (creator on 8 recordings), Frank Hummert (producer on 8 recordings), Jimmy Donnelly (performer on 8 recordings), Olive Lamoy (performer on 8 recordings), and Detmar Poppen (performer on 6 recordings).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Popeye radio preservation and duplicate transfers, children’s adventure comedy, Popeye / Thimble Theatre character property, food and strength gag, Wheatena-sponsored radio marketing, and non-OTR kiddie-record contamination.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Sparse survival and mixed-corpus contamination, 1935-1938 Popeye radio adaptations, Popeye debuts in Thimble Theatre, and Wheatena sponsorship changes Popeye food references.
